sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Madhurya Bhakti**: Meerabai practiced 'Madhurya Bhakti' (conjugal love), viewing herself as the 'Gopi' and Krishna as her eternal husband (Pati-Parmeshwar).
• **Social Rebellion**: She challenged the **Patriarchal norms** of the Rajput royalty by refusing to commit Sati and abandoning the 'Purdah' system to sing in public temples.
• **Literary Contribution**: Her compositions are known as **'Padavalis'**, written primarily in a blend of Brajbhasha and Rajasthani, characterized by intense emotional longing (Viraha).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Her life represents the intersection of **Vaishnavite theology** and the **Sufi-influenced** concept of 'Ishq-e-Haqiqi' (divine love).

items.definition: The specific form of Krishna worshipped by Meera, meaning 'the one who lifted the Govardhan mountain', symbolizing the protector of the devotee.
The lyrical poetry genre used by Meera; these songs were orally transmitted and later compiled, serving as a primary source for medieval linguistic evolution.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Social Empowerment**: Her life serves as a historical precedent for women's agency in the medieval period.
• **Cultural Synthesis**: Her works bridge the gap between folk traditions and classical Vaishnavite philosophy.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Historical authenticity of her life is often obscured by hagiographies (Bhaktamala).
• **Solutions**: Critical analysis of contemporary records (e.g., Nabhadas) vs. later oral traditions.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'M-R-K-D' (Meera, Rajput, Krishna, Dwarka).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Meera (Saint) - Rajput (Origin) - Krishna (Deity) - Dwarka (Final Abode).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Meera with the 'Varkari' tradition. Meera is NOT a Varkari saint; Varkari saints (Namdev, Tukaram) are associated with Vitthal (Pandharpur), not Krishna (Dwarka/Mathura).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Subaltern Agency' when discussing how Meera used Bhakti to bypass the rigid caste and gender hierarchies of the 16th-century Rajput court.

keyTakeaways: Meera represents the Saguna school of Bhakti, focusing on personal devotion to Krishna.
Her life was a direct challenge to the patriarchal structures of the Rajput feudal system.
Her poetry is a vital source for the study of medieval vernacular literature and the emotional landscape of the Bhakti movement.
